name: Stripe Managed Payments
summary: Stripe's Merchant of Record mode for eligible digital products, layered onto Stripe Payments and Checkout.

pricing.headline: 3.5% per Managed Payments transaction in addition to Stripe Payments fees.
pricing.assumptions: Illustrative US domestic-card total: 3.5% MoR fee plus 2.9% + $0.30 Payments fee. Stripe Billing adds 0.7% on pay-as-you-go subscriptions; disputes, other methods, international cards, and FX can add costs.

sellerCoverage: Public-preview eligibility is limited to Stripe's documented supported business locations.
buyerCoverage: Global buyer coverage excludes Stripe's documented restricted countries and varies by payment method.
products: Eligible digital products, SaaS, software, digital content, and virtual goods; services, physical goods, marketplaces, and many restricted categories are excluded.

features.checkout: Stripe Checkout, hosted or embedded, with Link as buyer-facing Merchant of Record.
features.subscriptions: Stripe Billing subscriptions with Managed Payments restrictions and public-preview changes.
features.invoicing: Managed receipts and invoices; several standalone and off-cycle invoice flows are restricted.
features.paymentMethods: Cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link, and selected local methods documented for Managed Payments.
features.payouts: Funds settle through the connected Stripe account subject to Stripe payout timing.

responsibilities.note: Stripe assumes the documented responsibilities for eligible Managed Payments transactions and supported markets, not every tax obligation everywhere.
Stripe and Link manage these transaction-level responsibilities.
The business retains product-level customer support.
Stripe can cancel subscriptions and delete related Stripe objects after a qualifying buyer request.

strengths: Small integration change for eligible Stripe Checkout users
Transaction-level choice between direct and MoR modes
limitations: MoR fee is additional to Payments and other applicable Stripe fees
bestFor: Teams wanting mixed MoR and direct transactions
avoidIf: You sell services, physical goods, or marketplace products
You require a generally available, long-established MoR product
